messages:
incidentbot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired: service=redwood-gpu-hosts, severity=page, incident=INC4951. Node: gpu-host-42 (rack-r7u3). Reason: KERNEL_PANIC detected by host-telemetry, kubelet: NotReady. Link: https://pagerduty.example/incidents/INC4951
alex kim: acked via PagerDuty. I'm on call — pulling serial console now. tagging @maria & @samir.
maria gonzalez: thanks alex. I'm checking hw telemetry + BMC. last serial dump shows ACPI reboot then oops. sharing logs in a sec.
infra-bot: host telemetry snapshot uploaded: s3://redwood-telemetry/gpu-host-42/4951236789.tar.gz
lia ng: ping: any immediate customer impact? any pods failed?
samir patel: looks like kubelet flapped. control-plane removed node from endpoints; some dedicated workloads on node were evicted. checking affected tenants.
alex kim: executing quick health check: `kubectl get node gpu-host-42 -o wide`
alex kim: ```
NAME         STATUS     ROLES    AGE   VERSION
gpu-host-42  NotReady   <none>   12d  v1.27.3
```
alex kim: `kubectl describe node gpu-host-42` shows kernel oops + kubelet lost heartbeat.
maria gonzalez: BMC shows last G3 -> ACPI powercycle at 03:12UTC, followed by kernel panic message: `Kernel panic - not syncing: Fatal exception` and nvme errors.
lia ng: customer impact: two Dedicated tenants (tenant-eta, tenant-sigma) had workloads on this host — their batches would have been retried but maybe increased latency. no active Hosted API endpoints were pinned to this node that I can see.
samir patel: marking tenant-eta as potentially impacted. I'll open a quick incident email thread if confirmed.
alex kim: attempting to connect serial console: `ipmitool -I lanplus -H bmc.gpu-host-42 -U admin -P **** sol activate`
alex kim: serial shows kernel panic stack and then watchdog reset. host didn't come back. I'm going to cordon the node to prevent new pods: `kubectl cordon gpu-host-42`
alex kim: `kubectl cordon gpu-host-42` -> node/gpu-host-42 cordoned
maria gonzalez: starting RMA intake ticket. likely NVMe or motherboard, but need full diagnostics. putting a hold on immediate reboots in case we want to capture more logs.
infra-bot: cold-boot attempt blocked by tag:do-not-reboot (reason: collect-core).
samir patel: evicting non-critical pods now to free capacity: `kubectl drain gpu-host-42 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force`
samir patel: drain output: ```
WARNING: ignoring DaemonSet-managed Pods: kube-system/nvidia-device-plugin
evicting pod tenant-eta/large-batch-processor-0 -> eviction succeeded
```
lia ng: tenant-sigma reports increased retry rate for model inferencing; latency spiked ~30% for a 5m window per our APM. tagging them in incident email.
maria gonzalez: any chance of graceful reboot bringing node back? recent kernel messages indicate nvme I/O parity errors, I lean toward RMA.
alex kim: since node is cordoned and drained, routing is stable. I'll start a replacement allocation from spare pool in rack-r7 to recover capacity for Dedicated customers.
samir patel: creating a temporary placement: `kubectl label node gpu-host-spare-01 spares=available && kubectl taint nodes --all node-role.kubernetes.io/spare-` (will adjust).
lia ng: notif: paging stakeholders. drafting short customer-facing blurb for tenant-eta & tenant-sigma: impact, mitigation, ETA for full capacity (TBD).
maria gonzalez: collecting serial console full dump and uploading to S3: s3://redwood-telemetry/gpu-host-42/4951236789/console.log
alex kim: handing off to second-line hw oncall @maria — I'll continue to watch kube events while you drive hardware path. If you want me to escalate to oncall-2, say so.
maria gonzalez: taking it. @samir if you need me to kick a remote power cycle after logs are captured, I'll authorize.
samir patel: please don't power cycle until we've exported kernel oops and `dmesg -T`. I'll continue to monitor scheduler stabilization and ensure auto-fallback of requests happened.
incidentbot: :white_check_mark: PagerDuty incident INC4951 acknowledged by alex kim
lia ng: note for postmortem: check our node placement logic — why were both tenant-eta workers on same physical host? consider affinity rules for dedicated workloads.
alex kim: good call. also check proactive alerts—why didn't nvme SMART warn earlier? opened an infra ticket to review disk telemetry thresholds.
maria gonzalez: RMA created: RMA-88921 against vendor, ETA part replacement 48-72h. tagging ops-runbook for on-prem team.
samir patel: mitigation summary: node cordoned+drained, spare node allocated to absorb capacity, tenant-eta & tenant-sigma experienced retries/latency spike but no data loss. customer notifications sent. open action items: (1) collect full kernel oops & dmesg, (2) review placement rules, (3) adjust nvme SMART thresholds, (4) add heartbeat escalation if multiple reboots detected within 10m.
alex kim: closing on-call loop: I'll update the incident doc with timeline and handoff notes, leaving this thread for follow-ups.
lia ng: thanks all :thumbsup: keep updates in the incident doc.
